publication.title: Spider2-V: How Far Are Multimodal Agents From Automating Data Science and Engineering Workflows?
publication.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems

name: Spider2-V: How Far Are Multimodal Agents From Automating Data Science and Engineering Workflows?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Benchmarks multimodal agents on data-science and engineering workflows involving enterprise applications, code, and GUI operations in real computer environments.

name: CAD-Assistant: Tool-Augmented VLLMs as Generic CAD Task Solvers
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: CAD-Assistant plans CAD tasks and executes actions through FreeCAD's Python API, using the changing design state to guide later commands.

name: ScienceBoard: Evaluating Multimodal Autonomous Agents in Realistic Scientific Workflows
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ScienceBoard combines an interactive environment with professional scientific software and 169 human-curated tasks in areas including biochemistry, astronomy, and geoinformatics. It evaluates computer-use agents on visually rich research workflows and analyzes their execution limitations.

name: VideoCAD: A Dataset and Model for Learning Long-Horizon 3D CAD UI Interactions from Video
notes: The contribution was reviewed from the retained abstract. Sections 1 and 3 of the exact-version v2 paper identify Onshape as the browser-based interaction environment; the use of pixel-level input does not make the operated surface a desktop application.
summary: Introduces synthetic CAD interaction videos, a model for learning interface actions from video, and evaluation tasks for spatial and long-horizon reasoning.

name: CODA: Coordinating the Cerebrum and Cerebellum for a Dual-Brain Computer Use Agent with Decoupled Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CODA combines a generalist planner with a specialist GUI executor and trains application-specific planners through decoupled GRPO. Successful specialist trajectories then support supervised training of a consolidated planner, evaluated across four ScienceBoard applications.

name: 3Dify: a Framework for Procedural 3D-CG Generation Assisted by LLMs Using MCP and RAG
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). GUI operation is a fallback within a 3D content-generation framework.
summary: Introduces 3Dify, a natural-language 3D graphics framework that operates creation tools through MCP and uses a computer-using agent for GUI operations when MCP is unavailable.

name: SheetBrain: A Neuro-Symbolic Agent for Accurate Reasoning over Complex and Large Spreadsheets
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces SheetBrain, a spreadsheet question-answering and manipulation agent that uses a Python sandbox and Excel tools, plus the SheetBench benchmark.

name: ProSoftArena: Benchmarking Hierarchical Capabilities of Multimodal Agents in Professional Software Environments
notes: The paper abstract and official full-text sections were reviewed. The full text supports Windows 11 virtual-machine execution, screenshot/state observations, and mouse/keyboard actions.
summary: ProSoftArena evaluates 436 professional-software tasks across six disciplines and 13 applications in a Windows 11 virtual-machine environment. Its capability hierarchy, execution-based checks, and human-in-the-loop evaluation cover precise GUI operations and multi-software workflows.

name: Exploring LLM Agent Designs and Interaction Modalities for Scientific Visualization
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This study compares specialized, computer-use and coding agents on scientific visualization workflows. It examines GUI, CLI, code and tool-call interaction modes, including how persistent memory changes performance across repeated trials.

name: MedCUA-Bench: A Screenshot-Only Benchmark for Clinical Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MedCUA-Bench evaluates screenshot-only clinical interface workflows using paired intent- and step-level goals. It combines reconstructed medical interfaces with completion and clinical-safety checks, and separately reports results on a real OpenEMR system.

name: ComAct: Reframing Professional Software Manipulation via COM-as-Action Paradigm
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ComAct proposes COM program synthesis as an alternative interface for manipulating professional software and introduces ComCADBench with GUI-based comparison agents. ComActor adds a staged training and correction approach, supported by a Windows-container training platform.

name: Running the Gauntlet: Hard Agentic Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v5). The benchmark uses five controlled web-based professional applications.
summary: Introduces GauntletBench, a web-based benchmark of vision-intensive tasks in five professional applications for assessing agent perception, 3D reasoning, and generalisation.

name: LabOSBench: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents for Scientific Instrument Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: LabOSBench evaluates GUI agents on browser-based scientific instrument simulators with configurable tasks and execution-based checks. Its subtask and end-to-end tests examine feedback-driven adjustment and long workflows without controlling physical instruments.

name: DSAgentBench: Can Agents Automate End-to-End Data-Science Workflows in Real Computer Environments?
notes: The paper abstract and official project README were reviewed. The README documents an Ubuntu desktop and GUI action interface and includes LLM-assisted evaluators; this annotation does not assert that every evaluator is deterministic.
summary: DSAgentBench evaluates end-to-end data-science workflows spanning analysis, modeling and visualization inside a real desktop environment. Task evaluators check produced analytical and visual artifacts, while the released interface supports screenshot or accessibility observations and GUI actions.

name: CADWorld: Computer-Use Benchmark for Long-Horizon Computer-Aided Design
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CADWorld evaluates screenshot-and-GUI agents on long FreeCAD workflows, from modeling and assembly to manufacturing and simulation. Executable checks inspect saved engineering artifacts for geometry, constraints, construction structure and downstream state.

name: MatToolBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents in Real-World Materials Science Workflows
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces MatToolBench, a Windows-based materials-science benchmark combining GUI operation, scientific-software scripting, and database queries. Expert-defined subcriteria support partial-credit scoring, while the evaluation examines domain knowledge gaps and cross-tool handoff failures.

name: EngiWorld: What Can Frontier Agents Deliver in Professional Engineering Environments?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces professional engineering tasks across software domains, with GUI and CLI access and artifact checks for geometric, physical, and design validity.

name: OSWorld-Science: A Benchmark of Computer Use Agents for Learning and Using Scientific Software
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Benchmarks computer agents on scientific-software workflows with task-specific checks of application states and generated research artifacts.

name: MedImageOSWorld: Benchmarking GUI Agents for Medical Image Consoles
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates GUI agents in simulated medical-imaging consoles, separately checking workflow completion and acquisition outcomes against hidden anatomical targets.

name: MAGAR: Multimodal Agents for GUI-Based 3D Mechanical Assembly and Minimal Rework
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported results use recorded states from held-out assembly families.
summary: Introduces MAGAR-Bench for GUI-based 3D mechanical assembly decisions and recovery, and MAGAR, a selective correction method for assembly outputs and actions.

name: ScienceCUA: Resource-to-Skill Construction and Execution-Guided Skill Evolution for Scientific Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces ScienceCUA, which turns scientific software documentation into reusable agent skills and revises them using execution feedback, with two audited evaluation variants.

name: Computer-Use Agents Gain Little Benefit from a World Model When Conditioned on Tutorials
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The finding concerns agents conditioned on tutorials, using OSWorld-Tutorial and ScienceBoard-Tutorial.
summary: RAG-PolicyJudge selects computer-use actions proposed with task-specific tutorials; the study compares its decisions with and without world-model rollouts.

counts.population: full benchmark reported in the paper, seven scientific domains

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Task-specific executable evaluators (JSON, CSV, artifact, R, SQL, Slicer and Praat checks plus author-provided scientific checks) inspect application states and collected deliverables and can award partial credit; the report command exports PASS/FAIL/VOID counts, scores, steps and costs.
benchmark_protocol.notes: The README states that 83.6% of tasks also allow CLI access and 16.4% are GUI-only under the recorded configurations. The published dataset includes answer keys (the private/ folder is hidden from the solver, not access-controlled), so results from models that may have trained on it are not held-out measurements. Record the code revision, task data revision, VM image, model and agent when comparing scores.

name: OSWorld-Science
notes: The repository holds the osworld_science package (CLI, VM control, agents, evaluators), VM build scripts and tests; task data and VM images are downloaded from the gated Hugging Face dataset, and the inspected tree contains no data/ files. The built-in prompt agent follows the OSWorld PromptAgent pattern (screenshot in, pyautogui code out); a Kimi tool-calling agent is vendored from xlang-ai/OSWorld under Apache-2.0. The paper builds task images on Ubuntu, and its ANSYS configuration runs on Windows; the README says that Windows image cannot be redistributed and the EEGLAB image is not yet published. The repository LICENSE is CC BY 4.0; scientific software and vendored components keep their own terms.
summary: Benchmark harness that runs computer-use agents on scientific-software tasks in per-domain VMs and scores the resulting application states and deliverables with task-specific executable evaluators.

name: GERALLT

summary: An LLM-driven system for testing RCE through its graphical interface, using separate models to control actions, assess problems, and describe icons.

name: grass-gui
notes: The ScienceBoard README lists this repository among its modified applications as the Python GUI part of GRASS GIS. Its manual.md installs GRASS 8.4 from the ubuntugis PPA and swaps this repository in for /usr/lib/grass84/gui/wxpython. At commit 4fe0312, wxgui.py starts a Flask thread on FLASK_PORT (default 8000) with /version, /init/cmd, /init/map, /init/layer, /init/scale, /dump, /gcmd, /gcmdline and /quit routes; /dump reports map layers, layer windows, toolbars, status-bar mode and scale, the region and console output. The rest of the tree is the upstream wxGUI code with its original README. GitHub does not mark the repository as a fork.
summary: ScienceBoard's replacement GRASS GIS 8.4 wxPython GUI with an embedded Flask server that loads mapsets and layers, runs GRASS commands and returns layer, region and console state as JSON for task checks.

name: kalgebra-kai
notes: GitHub reports this repository as a fork of KDE/kalgebra. The ScienceBoard README lists it among its modified applications as "a recompilation copy of KAlgebra". The Debian control file at commit e3f962b names the package kalgebra-kai (version 1.1) and describes it as a modified KAlgebra that supports a local server. main.cpp starts that server on the port given as the first argument (default 8000) with /version, /vars, /func/2d and /func/3d status routes and /tab, /add/calc, /add/2d and /add/3d operation routes. manual.md holds the maintainer's Qt 6.5 build and .deb packaging steps. Everything except the server additions is upstream KAlgebra code.
summary: Modified KAlgebra build from ScienceBoard with a local HTTP server that reports variables and plotted 2D and 3D functions and can switch tabs or add calculations and plots, so the benchmark can check math tasks.

name: ScaleCUA (THUDM) Qwen3-VL-8B ScienceBoard SFT
notes: Hub API at revision 48c39bb3 lists four BF16 safetensors shards (about 8.77B parameters) in the Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration architecture, plus a training-state file iter_0000494/common.pt; the repository is not gated. The card calls this the SFT start point used to initialize online RL and names Qwen3-VL-8B as its base without Hub base_model metadata, so base_model is unset. The card YAML declares license 'other' and its prose says the weights are released for research and inherit the base model's license; that license is not resolved here. The card reports no score for this checkpoint. The THUDM/SCALE-CUA README lists it among six SFT start-point checkpoints, each with a ModelScope mirror. This project is distinct from OpenGVLab/ScaleCUA.
summary: Supervised Qwen3-VL-8B checkpoint from THUDM's ScaleCUA, released as the start point that online RL initializes from for its ScienceBoard computer-use agent.

notes: Access requires manual approval by the publisher, so the dataset card and file contents were not read; the record rests on the public Hub metadata and file list, the paper and the benchmark README. The paper says the release holds all question sets and images and carries a contamination watermark; the benchmark README says it includes answer keys. summary: Gated Hub release of OSWorld-Science task definitions, staged inputs, grader references and prepared Ubuntu VM images for computer-use agents working in scientific software.

notes: Hub API at revision 3b089b66 lists five BF16 safetensors shards (about 10.29B parameters) in the Glm4vForConditionalGeneration architecture; the repository is not gated. The card calls this the online-RL (RLVR) checkpoint and names extreme1228/ScaleCUA-glm4.6v-scienceboard-sft as its start point, which is also its Hub base_model. The card and the THUDM/SCALE-CUA README report 49.4% on ScienceBoard; this is a publisher figure and was not reproduced. The card YAML declares license 'other' and its prose says the weights are released for research and inherit the license of GLM-4.6V-Flash; that license is not resolved here. The card states no parameter size, so no label is recorded. This project is distinct from OpenGVLab/ScaleCUA.
summary: GLM-4.6V-Flash computer-use agent checkpoint from THUDM's ScaleCUA, trained with online RL from a released SFT start point for ScienceBoard scientific-software tasks.
